questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates from Sihawa Mountain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Mahanadi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahanadi:**

 
 
• ​It originates from the Sihawa Mountain in the Dhamtari district of Chhattisgarh.
 
• The river originates from an extension of the Eastern Ghats.
 
• It flows in Odisha where it joins the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Other names of Mahanadi are Kanaknandini, Chitrapalal, Mahasweta, Nilotpala etc.
 
• Hirakud Dam is built on the Mahanadi.
 
• It is the largest earthen dam in the world.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Narmada:**

 
 
• ​The Narmada river originates from Amarkantak in the Anuppur district of Madhya Pradesh state in India.
 
• This River is also known as the Reva, and in ancient times it was also called Narbada (Nerbudda).
 
• The River Narmada is well known as the "Life Line of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh state".
 
• The total number of tributaries of the Narmada river is 41.
 
 
 
• Indus River:
 
 
• The river originates at Lake Mansarovar in Tibet (China).
 
• It drains Tibet (China), India and Pakistan.
 
• At last, the river falls into the Arabian Sea near Karachi (Pakistan).
 
• The length of the Indus is 3,180 km.
 
• **Rigvedic name of Indus is Sindhu.**
 
 
 
• Tributaries:__
 __
 
• ​__Left Bank: Zanskar, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.
 
• Right bank: Shyok, Gilgit, Hunza, Kabul, Swat, Kurram.
 
 
 
• Brahmaputra:
 __
 
• It originates under the name of Siang or Dihang, from the Angsi glacier__ of the Kailash range near the Mansarovar lake.
 
• It enters India west of Sadiya town in Arunachal Pradesh. 
 
 
 
• Tributaries: Dibang, Lohit, Siang, Burhi Dihing, Tista, and Dhansari.
 __
 
• It is known as Tsangpo in Tibet and Yarlung Zangbo in China. 
 
• The river crosses Assam below Dhubri and enters Bangladesh where the river is known as Jamuna and it flows for 337 km.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Respiratory failure is a condition in which your blood doesn't have enough _______ or has too much _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**oxygen; carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Respiratory failure **

 
 
• **Respiratory failure is a condition in which your blood doesn't have enough oxygen or has too much carbon dioxide.**
 
• Sometimes you can have both problems.
 
• When you breathe, your lungs take in oxygen. The oxygen passes into your blood, which carries it to your organs.
 
• Your organs, such as your heart and brain, need this oxygen-rich blood to work well.
 
• Another part of breathing is removing the carbon dioxide from the blood and breathing it out.
 
• Having too much carbon dioxide in your blood can harm your organs.
 
 
 
• **Causes of Respiratory Failure**
 
• Conditions that affect your breathing can cause respiratory failure.
 
• These conditions may affect the muscles, nerves, bones, or tissues that support breathing. The conditions are:
 
 
• Diseases that affect the lungs, such as COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), cystic fibrosis, pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, and COVID-19
 
• Conditions that affect the nerves and muscles that control breathing, such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), muscular dystrophy, spinal cord injuries, and stroke
 
• Problems with the spine, such as scoliosis (a curve in the spine). They can affect the bones and muscles used for breathing.
 
• Damage to the tissues and ribs around the lungs.
 
• An injury to the chest can cause this damage.
 
• Drug or alcohol overdose
 
• Inhalation injuries, such as from inhaling the smoke (from fires) or harmful fumes
 
 
 
• **Treatments for respiratory failure**
 
 
• Oxygen therapy
 
• Tracheostomy
 
• Ventilator
 
• Other breathing treatments, such as noninvasive positive pressure ventilation (NPPV),
 
• Fluids
 
• Medicines

questions.question: On the eve of which of the following festivals is Kotappakonda Fair of Andhra Pradesh organised?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Sri Trikoteswara Swamy temple** at **Kotappakonda hill **is one of the ancient and most famous temples in the district.

questions.question: How many hydrogen atoms does a molecule of acetic acid contain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical formula of Acetic acid is **CH₃COOH** or **C₂H₄O₂**.
 
• One molecule of acetic acid contains **4 Hydrogen atoms**. (2 Carbon and 2 Oxygen atoms)
 
• It is also called **Ethanoic acid**.
 
• It is the second simplest **form of carboxylic acid** (after Formic acid).
 
• **Vinegar has acetic acid** as its main component.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formic Acid** 

 
 
• The chemical formula is **HCOOH **or** CH₂O₂**
 
• It is found in **ant bites and insect stings.**
 
• This is a chemical defence mechanism found in insects.
 
 
 
• **Butyric acid **
 
 
• Its chemical formula is **CH₃(CH₂)₂COOH**
 
• It is found in butter-related products.

questions.question: Kalinga is present-day coastal _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalinga**

 
 
• Kalinga is a historical region of India.
 
• It is generally defined as the eastern coastal region **between the Mahanadi and the Godavari rivers**, although its boundaries have fluctuated with the territory of its rulers.
 
• Kalinga, an ancient territorial subdivision of east-central India.
 
• It corresponds to present-day northern Telangana, northeastern Andhra Pradesh, most of Odisha, and a portion of Madhya Pradesh states.
 
• **The core territory of Kalinga now encompasses a large part of Odisha**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Kalinga**
 
 
• Kalinga was conquered by Mahapadma, the founder of the Nanda dynasty of Magadha.
 
• It seceded from the Magadhan empire sometime after the fall of the Nanda dynasty
 
• But it was reconquered by the Mauryan king Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE in a terrible war that was said to have helped to convert him to Buddhism.
 
• **Ashoka’s 13th Rock Edict describes the Kalinga war vividly**.
 
• In about **263 BC Ashoka converted to Buddhism**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Governor: Ganeshi Lal
 
• Lok Sabha Seats: 21
 
• Rajya Sabha Seats: 10
 
• National parks: Bhitarkanika National Park, Similipal National Park
 
• Tiger Reserve: Satkosia TR, Similipal TR
 
 
 
• M Venkaiah Naidu, Vice President of India has presented the** Kalinga Ratna Samman for the year 2021** to **Biswabhusan Harichandan**, governor of Andhra Pradesh to recognize his contribution to** literature.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] In News__**

 
• **Jagdeep Dhankhar** is the** 14th **and current** vice president of India** replacing Venkaiah Naidu since 11 August 2022.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Indian Universities Act passed during the tenure of Lord Curzon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1904.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Indian University Act 1904

 
 
• The first provision of this act was that the governing bodies of the universities were to be reconstituted
 
• For the Universities of Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras, the elected fellows were to be 50 and for the rest of the universities, the number was fixed at 15.
 
• This act allowed the Government to appoint a majority of the fellows in a university.
 
• The Governor-General was now empowered to decide a University’s territorial limits and also affiliation between the universities and colleges.
 
• **The Indian Universities Act made the universities and colleges completely under Government's control.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Reforms and Administration under Lord Curzon (1899-1905)

 
 
• North-West Frontier Policy
 
• Afghan Policy
 
• Culcutta corporation Act,1899
 
• Andrew Frazer Commission, 1902
 
• **Introduction of Provincial Police Service**
 
• University Commission, 1902
 
• **University Act, 1904**
 
• Ancient Monuments Act, 1904
 
• **Partition of Bengal, 1905**

questions.question: According to guidelines by the RBI (as of January 2022), how many payment banks currently active in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ​A committee headed by Dr Nachiket Mor in 2013 recommended setting up of 'Payments Bank' to cater to the lower-income groups and small businesses.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India has formed Payment Banks to facilitate **more transaction and savings accounts** for the underserved population who lack banking access.
 
• Payment Banks will assist those who have **little or no banking access **and **allow increased access to financial services.**
 
• **Currently,** there are **6 active payments banks in India:**
 
 
• ** Airtel Payments Bank**
 
• **India Post Pay ments Bank**
 
• **Fino Payments Bank**
 
• **Jio Payments Bank**
 
• **Paytm Payments Bank**
 
• **NSDL Payments Bank**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Payment Banks** are registered under the** Companies Act 2013** but are governed by a host of legislations such as **Banking Regulation Act, 1949; RBI Act, 1934; Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 etc.**
 
• Main features of Payment Banks:-
 
 
• Acceptance of demand deposit is restricted to holding a maximum balance of Rs 200,000 per individual customer. 
 
• While the payment banks can't issue credit cards, they can issue ATM and debit cards.
 
• They are not allowed to give loans. 
 
• Distribution of non-risk sharing simple financial products like mutual fund units and insurance products, etc.
 
 
• They are only allowed to invest the money received from customers' deposits into government securities.
 
 
 
• They cannot accept NRI deposits.

questions.question: The Composition of the Council of States comes under the purview of which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**80.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rajya Sabha or Council of States is the upper house of the Parliament of India.**
 
• Composition/Strength of Rajya Sabha:
 
 
• Article 80 of the Constitution lays down the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha as 250.
 
• Out of 250 seats of Rajya Sabha, 12 members are nominated by the President and 238 are representatives of the States and of the two Union Territories. 
 
• The present strength of Rajya Sabha is 245, out of which 233 are representatives of the States and Union territories of Delhi and Puducherry and 12 are nominated by the President.
 
• The members nominated by the President are persons having special knowledge or practical experience in respect of such matters as literature, science, art and social service. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Rajya Sabha (Council of States):

 
 
• The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for the creation of a ‘Council of State’ as a second chamber of the then legislature.
 
• Rajya Sabha is the Upper house of the bicameral Parliament of India.
 
• Allocation of Seats:
 
 
• The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution provides for the allocation of seats to the States and Union Territories in Rajya Sabha. 
 
• The allocation of seats is made on the basis of the population of each State.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lok Sabha:

 
 
• Lok Sabha is composed of representatives of the people chosen by direct election on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• Article 81 of the Constitution defines the composition of the House of the People or Lok Sabha.
 
• The maximum strength of the House envisaged by the Constitution is 552.
 
• Out of 552 seats of Lok Sabha:
 
 
• Up to 530 members represent the States
 
• Up to 20 members represent the Union Territories
 
• Not more than two members of the Anglo-Indian Community to be nominated by the president if this community is not adequately represented in the House. 
 
 
 
• The house currently has 543 seats, which are filled by the election of up to 543 elected members.

questions.question: Who among the following made the statement: "one caste, one religion, one god for humankind"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Shri Narayana Guru.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shri Narayana Guru**, a guru from the **Ezhava caste** in present-day **Kerala **proclaimed the ideals of unity for his people.
 
• He argued against treating people unequally on the basis of caste differences.
 
• According to him, **all humankind belonged to the same caste. **
 
• **"Oru jati, oru matam, oru daivam manushyanu” (One caste, one religion, one god for humankind) is one of his famous statements. **
 
• The **Sri Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP)** **movement**, among the Ezhavas of Kerala, is an example of a conflict between the depressed classes and the upper non-Brahmana castes.
 
• **The Ezhavas were a caste of toddy-tappers in Kerala.** They were like the Nadars of Tamil Nadu and the Idigas of Karnataka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Ghasidas **

 
 
• ​The most-important **Satnami group** was founded in **1820 in the Chattisgarh **region of middle India by Ghasidas, a farm servant and member of the Chamar caste.
 
• His **Satnam Panth (“Path of the True Name”)** succeeded in providing a religious and social identity for large numbers of Chattisgarhi Chamars.
 
• Ghasidas is remembered for having thrown images of Hindu gods onto a rubbish heap.
 
• He preached a code of ethical and dietary self-restraint and social equality.
 
 
 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswati **
 
 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** founded the Arya Samaj.
 
• Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875.
 
• He translated the Vedas and wrote three books named **Satyartha Prakash, Veda Bhasya Bhumika, and Veda Bhasya.**
 
• He gave the slogan **“Go back to Vedas”.**
 
• Dayanand Anglo Vedic **(D.A.V) **schools were established based on his philosophy and teachings.

questions.question: When do we celebrate National Press Day in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16 November.** __

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Press Day** is observed on the **16th of November.**
 
• This was the day on which the **Press Council of India started functioning** as a moral watchdog.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PCI (Press Council of India)**

 
 
• It **started** functioning on **16 November 1966.**
 
• It is a **statutory**, **self-regulatory** and **autonomous body** formed to **regulate the media** in India.
 
• It works under the **Press Council Act 1978**.
 
• The structure of PCI consists of **a chairman and a 28-member committee** with a variety of representatives from journalists, News agencies, Media managers and Members of Parliament.
 
• The **committee is headed by a chairman** who is usually a retired Supreme court judge selected by a 3-member committee(Speaker of LS, Chairman of RS, a member of PCI.)

questions.question: World Alzheimer's Day is observed on _______ globally every year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21 September**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Alzheimer’s Day**

 
 
• **It is celebrated on September 21 each year.**
 
• On this day, the world concentrates its efforts on creating awareness of Alzheimer’s disease.
 
• The disease is among the most prevalent forms of dementia, a set of disorders that disrupt mental function.
 
• World Alzheimer’s Day is the perfect opportunity for us to raise our voices and find new ways of fighting the disease’s effects
 
• Alzheimer’s is a form of dementia that affects memory and impairs daily function.
 
• It is responsible for somewhere between 60% and 80% of dementia cases.
 
• The first ‘World Alzheimer Report’ was launched in 2009 on World Alzheimer’s Day and yearly reports have been issued every year since

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Government of India appoint the Saddler University Commission to analyse the problems of the Calcutta University?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1917.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saddler Commission** was set up in **1917** to **study and report on problems of Calcutta University**.
 
• It analysed the conditions prevailing in the educational system and suggested some measures, submitting its report in 1919.
 
• It recommended a separate board for secondary and intermediate education
 
• It stated that the improvement of secondary education was a necessary condition for the improvement of University education.
 
• It recommended that Universities should be freed from excessive official control.
 
• It stressed the teacher education and organising the teaching staff.
 
• It also recommended the provision of a three-year degree course after the intermediate stage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Woods Despatch (1854)**

 
 
• It is called the Magna Carta of education in India.
 
• It is the first major policy that advocated the system of education at various levels and in an organised manner.
 
 
 
• **Hunter Commission (1882-83)**
 
 
• Its recommendations are mainly related to primary and secondary education.

questions.question: How many sections are there in the Government of India Act, 1935?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**321**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government of India act 1935 was passed by the British Parliament in August 1935.With 321 sections and 10 schedules.
 
• This was the longest act passed by the British Parliament so far and was later split into two parts viz. **Government of India act 1935 and Government of Burma act 1935.**
 
• The Government of India acts in 1935 derived material from four key sources viz. Report of the Simon Commission, discussions at the third round table conference.
 
• The White paper of 1933, and the reports of the Joint select committees.
 
• The act ended the system of dyarchy introduced by the GOI act 1919 and provided for the establishment of a Federation of India to be made of provinces of British India and some or all of the Princely states. However, the federation never came into being as the required number of princely states did not join it.
 
• **Lord Linlithgow** was the viceroy of India when the Government of India Act of 1935 was passed.
 
• Most of the features of the Government of India Act of 1935 are borrowed for making the Indian Constitution.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Major Provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935

 
 
• **Established Provincial autonomy**
 
• **Diarchy is abolished in provinces and introduced in the Center**
 
• **Bicameral Legislature is introduced in Parliament**
 
• **Establishment of RBI.**
 
• **Federal Court in 1937.**
 
• **Introduced direct elections in India for the first time.**
 
• **A Federal Railway Authority was set up to control Indian railways.**
 
• **The Act also provided for the establishment of federal, provincial, and joint Public Service Commissions. **

questions.question: Two women mountaineers, Gunbala Sharma and _______ became the first Indian women to summit Mount Pumori (7,161 metres) in Nepal on 12 May 2021.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baljeet Kaur.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Baljeet Kaur** and **Gunbala Sharma** are the **first Indian women** to **scale Mt. Pumori**.
 
• They have reached their peak on May 12 2021.
 
• **Baljeet Kaur** is from **Himachal Pradesh** and **Gunbala Sharma** is from **Rajasthan**.
 
• **Mount Pumori** is one of the **toughest peaks in the Everest Massif** in Nepal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Everest Massif** is a closely **packed group of mountains** with peaks other than Everest.
 
• The peaks in the massif are **Mt Nuptse**, **Mt Pumori**, **Mt Lhotse** and **Mt Everest**, all in Nepal.
 
• Some of the peaks in the massif are considered to be tougher than climbing Everest.
 
• First **Indian woman** to climb **Mt Everest**: **Bachendri Pal.**
 
• **Youngest girl** to climb **Mt Everest**: **Malavath Purna.**
